The source (.github/scripts/release_closeout.py) was read first to confirm the shape of the expected failure: run_tag_mode() first checks TAG_SHAPE_RE (v1.1.0 matches -> PASS), then calls read_at_tag(tag, 'NIZAM.json'), which shells out to `git show v1.1.0:NIZAM.json`; because no such tag exists, `git show` returns non-zero, read_at_tag returns None (it does not distinguish tag-absent from file-absent-at-tag), and the next `require(...)` call prints a named `FAIL NIZAM.json readable at v1.1.0 (V reference)` and calls sys.exit(1) -- a clean, named, first-failure-semantics FAIL, never an uncaught exception and never a silent PASS. This is the PASS condition for the check: it proves the tag-mode gate cannot be spoofed by this contract's prepared-but-untagged v1.1.0 anchor set -- the gate reads the tag's own committed content via `git show`, not the working tree, so no amount of working-tree anchor preparation can make tag mode succeed before the tag genuinely exists.
